A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the FID navigator can be used as a reliable motion monitor for prospective correction, that the image navigator can be acquired on‐demand and that this combination is robust against motion.
FID‐guided image navigators are a promising concept for prospective motion correction.
we are able to use the FID signal for prospective motion correction, and that we can use this method to reduce motion artifacts for both 1D and 2D image navigators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of FID navigators to detect motion is not only feasible, but can also guide the acquisition of high‐quality image navigators.
FID navigators are a promising tool for prospective motion correction, and that they can be used to guide on‐demand navigator acquisitions for motion correction in the presence of motion.

FID‐guided prospective motion correction using on‐demand navigators can be implemented on existing clinical MR systems without the need for additional hardware and that this approach can be used for motion correction in the presence of motion that is slow, fast, periodic, or a combination of all three.
